turns.text: it's almost 4 and i'm up. my boyfriend Tomás moves in tomorrow, wednesday is when things settle but tonight is the night before. i work mon/tue/wed/sat nights this stretch so i'm on shift tomorrow night too. need a short plan for tonight + a little care package for him, and quiet hours setup so my sleep is protected. i sleep 8:30 to 3 with blackout curtains and the box fan. ok but realistically keep it short

Quick plan, built around your 8:30-3 sleep window and four nights a week.

**Tonight (before he arrives)**
- Clear one shelf in the fridge and one drawer or closet section for Tomás.
- Wash a set of sheets so the bed is ready.
- Pack your shift bag and thermos now so you're not rattling around tomorrow.

**Care package (cheap, 10 min)**
- Spare key on a tag
- A pair of earplugs
- Snacks he likes plus a bottle of water
- Sticky note with wifi password and where the trash goes

**Quiet-hours setup**
- Agree on 8:30 a.m.-3 p.m. as quiet after your shifts: no vacuum, no speakerphone, shoes off in the hall.
- Put a small sign or a text-me rule on the bedroom door.
- Keep blackout curtains and the box fan as is.
- Since you work Mon/Tue/Wed/Sat, put those nights on a shared calendar so he knows which mornings are quiet ones.

Want a one-line version for the sticky note?

yes pls. also the baby next door cries thru the 207/209 wall, i wear earplugs and white noise. i made a white noise + soothing playlist for the parents there. can i make it more useful than just a link to them?

Yes, turn it into a small ready-to-use kit.

**Sticky note for Tomás:** "Quiet 8:30-3 after her shifts. Shoes off, low volume, text don't call. Thanks!"

**Making the playlist practical for your neighbors**
- Split it into two: a 45-minute nap playlist and a 3-hour overnight loop, so they can press play without picking.
- Name them plainly, like "Nap" and "Overnight".
- Keep tracks gapless and with no ads, and note the best volume so it masks sound without being loud.
- Add a QR code on a small card so they can scan it with one hand. Put it on their door with a short note: "Hope this helps with sleep. No need to reply."
- Optional: a pair of foam earplugs or a cheap sound machine setting suggestion in the card.

I can draft the card text if you'd like.
"Two playlists for naps and nights, scan and press play. Hope you all get some sleep. No need to reply! - [your name], next door"
